summary: @onereach/step-conversation preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: Package's `preinstall` hook runs `setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (v1.3.13), extracts and chmod +x's it in a temp directory, and uses it to execute the bundled `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle with obfuscator.io-style hex-encoded identifiers, a ~1000-entry rotated string array, and a `WV8StW` string-array-shuffle routine designed to defeat static review. The `setup.mjs` lifecycle script itself is variable-name-obfuscated with `_0xNNNNNN` identifiers and property-alias tables. The declared package purpose is a small conversation-step class library (`dst/step.js`, ~10KB), which has no need for a second language runtime or a megabyte-scale opaque payload. Fetching an alien runtime at install time solely to execute a bundled obfuscated payload matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern rather than legitimate native-build tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
